what: The constructor discovers positive loc and visited facts from semantic fact names, infers the unique depot as the non-customer location, and builds task-independent customer mappings. It identifies the metric-cost numeric target from return-to-depot effects and reconstructs every directed travel cost from the grounded visit and return-to-depot operators using assignment-effect right-hand-side initial values. At evaluation time it reads the propositional state once, finds the current location and unvisited customers, then combines a directed nearest-neighbor completion ending at the depot with an MST-based endpoint estimate over the unvisited customers. Reusable buffers avoid per-state large allocations.
why: CVRP states are primarily distinguished by the current endpoint and the subset of customers still unvisited, while all remaining movement costs are static and recoverable from grounded operators. A nearest-neighbor completion provides inexpensive, route-sensitive guidance that favors spatially coherent customer sequences; the MST component reduces the instability and myopia of the greedy completion. The design deliberately avoids fragile parsing of derived numeric expressions and does not depend on unavailable capacity or demand APIs, fixed IDs, customer names, symmetry, or instance size.
